title: Survive the reboot
briefing: nginx is running again — but you notice it isn't set to start at boot.
If app-01 reboots tonight, the site stays down until someone starts it by
hand. 'active' (running now) and 'enabled' (starts at boot) are separate.
tips: Check the boot setting with: systemctl is-enabled nginx.
`enable` wires a service to start automatically; `start` only affects right now.
objective: Make nginx start automatically on boot — leave it enabled.
expert_objective: Ensure nginx comes up on its own after a reboot.
hints: Confirm the problem: `systemctl is-enabled nginx` prints 'disabled'.
Wire it to boot: `sudo systemctl enable nginx`.
`sudo systemctl enable nginx` — it creates a symlink into multi-user.target.wants.
solution:
systemctl is-enabled nginx
sudo systemctl enable nginx
explanation: enable and start solve different problems. `start` runs a service now; `enable` makes systemd start it on every boot. Production services almost always want both — running today, and running again after the next reboot.
